questions.prompt: Do you usually notice small details in places you visit?
questions.sampleA1: No, I don't notice. I see big things. Not small things.
questions.sampleA2: I don't see small details. But I see big things. And I like places.
questions.sampleB1: I don't usually notice small details. I look at the big things. However, if something is very strange, I see it. For example, if a wall is a strange color. I prefer to see the whole place.
questions.sampleB2: To be honest, not really — I tend to take in the overall feel of a place rather than the little things. That said, if something really stands out, like a quirky sign or an odd bit of decoration, it'll catch my eye straight away. I suppose I'm more of a big-picture person.

questions.uzSampleB1: Men odatda kichik detallarga e'tibor bermayman. Men katta narsalarga qarayman. Biroq, agar biror narsa juda g'alati bo'lsa, men uni ko'raman. Misol uchun, agar devor g'alati rangda bo'lsa. Men butun joyni ko'rishni afzal ko'raman.
questions.uzSampleB2:
Men odatda biror joyga borganimda kichik detallarga e'tibor bermayman. Men ko'proq umumiy taassurotga e'tibor qarataman.
Biroq, agar biror narsa juda g'ayrioddiy yoki hayratlanarli bo'lsa, u mening e'tiborimni tortadi.
Misol uchun, g'alati san'at asari yoki qiziqarli arxitektura detali.

vocabulary.title: Do you usually...
idioms: miss the forest for the trees - "o'rmonni daraxtlar uchun o'tkazib yubormoq"

questions.sampleAnswer:
To be honest, I wouldn't say I'm particularly observant of minute details in new places. I tend to focus on the bigger picture, the overall atmosphere and impression a place gives me. That being said, if something is particularly striking or out of place, it will definitely jump out at me. For example, an unusual architectural feature or a particularly vibrant piece of street art.

Generally speaking, I think I'm more attuned to the emotional vibe of a location than the specific physical elements. I might not remember the exact color of the walls, but I'll remember how the place made me feel. It's more about the experience as a whole, rather than the sum of its parts. It's like the forest for the trees, I guess.
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Rostini aytsam, men yangi joylardagi mayda detallarga ayniqsa e'tibor beraman deb ayta olmayman. Men ko'proq katta manzara, joyning umumiy muhiti va taassurotiga e'tibor qarataman. Shunga qaramay, agar biror narsa ayniqsa hayratlanarli yoki o'z o'rnida bo'lmasa, u albatta ko'zimga tashlanadi. Misol uchun, g'ayrioddiy arxitektura elementi yoki ko'cha san'atining ayniqsa yorqin namunasi.

Umuman olganda, menimcha, men joyning aniq jismoniy elementlaridan ko'ra ko'proq hissiy kayfiyatiga moslashganman. Men devorlarning aniq rangini eslay olmasligim mumkin, lekin bu joy menga qanday ta'sir qilganini eslayman. Bu ko'proq butun tajriba haqida, uning qismlari yig'indisidan ko'ra. Bu, menimcha, daraxtlar orasida o'rmonni ko'rishga o'xshaydi.

questions.sampleA1: Yes, I like museums. I see old things. They are good.
questions.sampleA2: I like museums. And I see old things. But sometimes they are boring.
questions.sampleB1: I like museums. I can see old things. For example, old cars or old clothes. However, sometimes they are boring. There are too many people.
questions.sampleB2: Yeah, I'm quite keen on museums, to be honest. There's something special about seeing a real artefact up close rather than in a textbook. I suppose art and history ones are more my cup of tea — science museums can drag on a bit. All in all, though, they're a brilliant way to soak up a bit of culture.
questions.uzSampleA1: Ha, menga muzeylar yoqadi. Men eski narsalarni ko'raman. Ular yaxshi.
questions.uzSampleA2:
Men muzeylarni yaxshi ko'raman.
Va men eski narsalarni ko'raman.
Lekin ba'zida ular zerikarli bo'ladi.
questions.uzSampleB1:
Menga muzeylar yoqadi. Men eski narsalarni ko'rishim mumkin.
Masalan, eski mashinalar yoki eski kiyimlar.
Biroq, ba'zida ular zerikarli bo'ladi. Juda ko'p odam bor.
questions.uzSampleB2:
Men muzeylarga borishni yoqtiraman, lekin bu muzeyning turiga bog'liq. Men ko'proq san'at muzeylari va tarix muzeylaridan zavqlanaman.
Biroq, fan muzeylari menga unchalik yoqmaydi. Men ularni biroz zerikarli deb bilaman. Menimcha, madaniyatga sho'ng'ish muhim va muzeylar buning uchun ajoyib usuldir.
questions.sampleAnswer:
I have a somewhat complicated relationship with museums. On the one hand, I appreciate the opportunity to engage with art, history, and culture in a tangible way. There's something special about seeing a historical artifact or a famous painting in person, rather than just in a book or online. Moreover, museums can be great places to learn and expand your knowledge.

However, I also find that museums can sometimes be overwhelming. The crowds, the noise, and the sheer volume of information can be exhausting. I often find myself zoning out after a couple of hours. It's a mixed bag, really. I think it really depends on the specific museum and my mood on the day. Essentially, I can take it or leave it.
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Mening muzeylar bilan munosabatim biroz murakkab. Bir tomondan, men san'at, tarix va madaniyat bilan aniq tarzda tanishish imkoniyatini qadrlayman. Tarixiy artefaktni yoki mashhur rasmni kitobda yoki onlaynda emas, balki shaxsan ko'rishda o'zgacha bir narsa bor. Qolaversa, muzeylar bilim olish va uni kengaytirish uchun ajoyib joy bo'lishi mumkin.

Biroq, men shuni ham bilamanki, muzeylar ba'zan haddan tashqari bosim o'tkazishi mumkin. Olomon, shovqin va ma'lumotlarning haddan tashqari ko'pligi charchatadi. Ko'pincha bir necha soatdan keyin diqqatimni yo'qotaman. Aslida, bu aralash tuyg'ular. Menimcha, bu aniq muzeyga va o'sha kundagi kayfiyatimga bog'liq. Asosan, men uni qabul ham qila olaman, rad ham eta olaman.

questions.prompt: Do you prefer reading books or watching videos to learn something?
questions.sampleA1: I like videos. Videos are good. Books are boring.
questions.sampleA2: I like videos. And they are fun. But books are boring.
questions.sampleB1: I prefer videos. Videos are more interesting than books. For example, I can see things. However, books have more information. It depends on what I want to learn.
questions.sampleB2: It depends, really, but on the whole I'd lean towards reading. The thing is, when I read I can go at my own pace and go back over anything that doesn't quite sink in. Videos are handy for picking things up quickly, I'll admit, but the information tends to wash over me. So books win it for me.
questions.uzSampleA1: Menga videolar yoqadi. Videolar yaxshi. Kitoblar zerikarli.
questions.uzSampleA2: Menga videolar yoqadi. Va ular qiziqarli. Lekin kitoblar zerikarli.
questions.uzSampleB1:
Men videolarni afzal ko'raman. Videolar kitoblarga qaraganda qiziqarliroq.
Misol uchun, men narsalarni ko'rishim mumkin.
Biroq, kitoblarda ko'proq ma'lumot bor. Bu men nimani o'rganmoqchiligimga bog'liq.
questions.uzSampleB2:
Men odatda nimadir o'rganish uchun kitob o'qishni afzal ko'raman. O'qiyotganimda yaxshiroq diqqatni jamlay olaman deb o'ylayman.
Qolaversa, tushunmagan joylarimni qayta ko'rib chiqishim mumkin.
Biroq, ba'zi odamlar videolarni afzal ko'rishlarini tushunaman. Bu haqiqatan ham sizning o'rganish uslubingizga bog'liq.

vocabulary.title: Do you prefer...
idioms: hit the nail on the head - "mixni boshiga urmoq"
different strokes for different folks - "har kimning o'z uslubi bor"
sentenceStarters: "I like... more than..." - "Men ... ni ... dan ko'ra ko'proq yoqtiraman"

questions.sampleAnswer:
Personally, I learn best by reading. While videos can be engaging and visually stimulating, I find that the information doesn't always sink in as deeply as when I read something. When I read, I can control the pace, go back over sections I don't understand, and make notes. It's a more active and immersive learning experience for me.

That being said, I recognize that videos have their own advantages. They can be particularly helpful for visual learners, and they can often explain complex concepts in a more accessible way. Ultimately, I think it comes down to individual learning styles and the subject matter at hand. Different strokes for different folks, as they say. But if I had to choose one, I'd lean towards reading. Knowledge is power, and reading unlocks it for me.
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Shaxsan men uchun o'qish orqali yaxshiroq o'rganaman. Videolar qiziqarli va vizual jihatdan rag'batlantiruvchi bo'lishi mumkin bo'lsa-da, menimcha, ma'lumotlar nimadir o'qiganimdagidek chuqur singib ketmaydi. O'qiganimda, men tempni nazorat qila olaman, tushunmagan qismlarimni qayta ko'rib chiqaman va eslatmalar yozib olaman. Bu men uchun yanada faol va chuqur o'rganish tajribasi.

Shuni aytishim kerakki, videolarning ham o'z afzalliklari borligini tan olaman. Ular, ayniqsa, vizual o'rganuvchilar uchun foydali bo'lishi mumkin va ular ko'pincha murakkab tushunchalarni yanada tushunarli tarzda tushuntirib berishlari mumkin. Oxir oqibat, menimcha, bu individual o'rganish uslublariga va qo'l ostidagi mavzuga bog'liq. Har kimning o'z didi bor, deyishadi. Ammo agar men birini tanlashim kerak bo'lsa, men o'qishga moyil bo'lardim. Bilim - kuch, va o'qish men uchun uni ochadi.

questions.sampleA1: One picture has people. The other picture has machines. The machines are big.
questions.sampleA2: One picture has people working. And the other picture has machines. The machines are faster but the people are working hard.
questions.sampleB1: In the first picture, people are picking crops. In the second picture, machines are picking crops. The machines are faster. For example, they can pick more crops in one day. However, the people are working hard. Both are harvesting.
questions.sampleB2: Both images clearly illustrate the process of harvesting crops, but they represent vastly different approaches. The first picture shows a group of farmers engaged in manual labour, likely harvesting rice in a paddy field. They are using traditional tools like sickles and carrying baskets, suggesting a more traditional farming method and a smaller scale operation, possibly in a developing country. In contrast, the second image presents a highly mechanised harvest. Here, several large combine harvesters and tractors are hard at work across expansive fields, showcasing modern, industrial-scale agriculture. It's a striking comparison between age-old practices and cutting-edge technology in food production.
questions.uzSampleA1: Birinchi rasmda odamlar bor. Ikkinchi rasmda mashinalar bor. Mashinalar katta.
questions.uzSampleA2:
Birinchi rasmda odamlar ishlayapti.
Ikkinchi rasmda esa mashinalar bor. Mashinalar tezroq, lekin odamlar qattiq mehnat qilyapti.

Birinchi rasmda odamlar hosil yig'ishtirmoqda. Ikkinchi rasmda esa mashinalar hosil yig'ishtirmoqda. Mashinalar tezroq.
Masalan, ular bir kunda ko'proq hosil yig'ishtirishi mumkin.
Biroq, odamlar qattiq mehnat qilmoqda. Ikkalasi ham hosilni terib olishmoqda.

Mashinalar ancha tezroq va samaraliroq. Biroq, birinchi rasmdagi odamlar, ehtimol, tirikchilik qilyapti. Bu samaradorlik va bandlik masalasidir. Bu texnologiya va an'analar o'rtasidagi kurashga borib taqaladi.

vocabulary.title: Describe these...
idioms: the best of both worlds - "ikkala dunyoning eng yaxshisi"
sentenceStarters: "In the first picture, I see..." - "Birinchi rasmda men ... ni ko'ryapman"
"In the second picture, there is..." - "Ikkinchi rasmda ... bor"

questions.sampleAnswer:
Alright, in the first picture, we see a field where people are harvesting crops by hand. It looks like a labor-intensive process, and it probably requires a significant amount of manpower to cover even a relatively small area. Presumably, this is happening in a region where labor costs are low and access to modern machinery is limited. The workers seem to be working hard under what appear to be difficult conditions.

In contrast, the second picture shows a vast field being harvested by large, sophisticated machines. These machines are likely capable of harvesting enormous quantities of crops in a fraction of the time it would take a team of manual laborers. Clearly, this represents a more efficient and technologically advanced approach to agriculture. Moreover, it reduces the need for manual labor, but it also raises questions about employment and the socioeconomic impact of automation. It's a world apart, showing two very different approaches to farming.

Ultimately, both methods serve the same purpose – to harvest crops and provide food. However, they reflect vastly different levels of technological development and economic circumstances. The manual labor approach is likely more sustainable in some ways, while the mechanized approach is more productive. You reap what you sow, regardless of the method.
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Xo'sh, birinchi rasmda biz odamlarning qo'lda hosil yig'ishtirayotgan dalasini ko'ramiz. Bu mehnat talab qiladigan jarayonga o'xshaydi va hatto nisbatan kichik maydonni qoplash uchun ham sezilarli miqdorda ishchi kuchi talab qilishi mumkin. Ehtimol, bu mehnat xarajatlari past va zamonaviy texnikaga kirish imkoniyati cheklangan hududda sodir bo'lmoqda. Ishchilar qiyin sharoitlarda qattiq mehnat qilayotganga o'xshaydi.

Aksincha, ikkinchi rasmda katta, murakkab mashinalar yordamida hosil yig'ishtirilayotgan keng dala ko'rsatilgan. Bu mashinalar, ehtimol, qo'lda ishlaydigan ishchilar guruhiga ketadigan vaqtning bir qismida juda katta miqdordagi hosilni yig'ishtirishga qodir. Shubhasiz, bu qishloq xo'jaligiga nisbatan ancha samarali va texnologik jihatdan rivojlangan yondashuvni anglatadi. Bundan tashqari, u qo'l mehnati zaruratini kamaytiradi, lekin u bandlik va avtomatlashtirishning ijtimoiy-iqtisodiy ta'siri haqida savollar tug'diradi. Bu butunlay boshqa dunyo, dehqonchilikka ikki xil yondashuvni ko'rsatadi.

Oxir oqibat, ikkala usul ham bir xil maqsadga xizmat qiladi – hosil yig'ishtirish va oziq-ovqat bilan ta'minlash. Biroq, ular texnologik rivojlanish va iqtisodiy sharoitlarning juda katta farqini aks ettiradi. Qo'l mehnati yondashuvi ba'zi jihatlarda yanada barqaror bo'lishi mumkin, mexanizatsiyalashgan yondashuv esa unumliroqdir. Nima eksang, shuni o'rasan, usulidan qat'i nazar.

questions.prompt: What are the advantages of using machines in farming?
questions.sampleA1: Machines are good. They help farmers. Work is faster.
questions.sampleA2: Machines help farmers. They work fast and it is easy. But machines are expensive.
questions.sampleB1: Machines in farming are very helpful. They make work faster and easier. For example, a tractor can plow a field much quicker than a person. However, machines can be expensive to buy and maintain. They also need fuel to operate. So, there are both good and bad things about using machines.
questions.sampleB2: Well, the big plus is efficiency — machines can cover a huge area in no time, which really cuts down on labour. On top of that, they take a lot of the back-breaking work off people's shoulders. And with modern tech like GPS, farmers can be far more precise, which ends up boosting yields and cutting waste.
questions.uzSampleA1: Mashinalar yaxshi. Ular fermerlarga yordam beradi. Ish tezroq bo'ladi.
questions.uzSampleA2: Mashinalar fermerlarga yordam beradi. Ular tez ishlaydi va bu oson. Lekin mashinalar qimmat turadi.
questions.uzSampleB1:
Qishloq xo'jaligida mashinalar juda foydali. Ular ishni tezroq va osonroq qiladi.
Masalan, traktor dalani odamga qaraganda ancha tezroq hayday oladi.
Biroq, mashinalarni sotib olish va ularga xizmat ko'rsatish qimmat bo'lishi mumkin. Ular, shuningdek, ishlash uchun yoqilg'iga muhtoj. Shunday qilib, mashinalardan foydalanishning ham yaxshi, ham yomon tomonlari bor.
questions.uzSampleB2:
Qishloq xo'jaligida mashinalardan foydalanish bir nechta asosiy afzalliklarni taqdim etadi. Ular samaradorlikni sezilarli darajada oshiradi, bu fermerlarga kamroq vaqt ichida ko'proq yer maydonini qamrab olish imkonini beradi.
Bundan tashqari, mashinalar jismoniy jihatdan og'ir va ko'p vaqt talab qiladigan qo'l mehnatiga bo'lgan ehtiyojni kamaytiradi.
Bundan tashqari, mashinalardagi texnologiya orqali ta'minlangan aniq dehqonchilik usullari resurslardan foydalanishni yaxshilaydi va chiqindilarni kamaytiradi.
Natijada, bu yuqori hosildorlikka va yanada barqaror qishloq xo'jaligi amaliyotlariga olib keladi.

vocabulary.title: What are...
idioms: make hay while the sun shines - "quyosh charaqlab turganda pichanni o'rib qol"
the best of both worlds - "ikki dunyoning yaxshiligi"
sentenceStarters: "Machines allow farmers to..." - "Mashinalar fermerlarga imkon beradi..."

questions.sampleAnswer:
The advantages of using machines in farming are numerous and ultimately contribute to increased efficiency and productivity. Firstly, machines like tractors and combine harvesters can cover vast areas of land much faster than manual labor, enabling farmers to plant and harvest crops in a timely manner, making hay while the sun shines. This is particularly crucial during peak seasons when time is of the essence.

Secondly, machines reduce the physical strain on farmers and agricultural workers. Tasks that would otherwise require back-breaking labor can be completed with relative ease using machinery. Furthermore, the precision offered by modern farming equipment minimizes waste and maximizes yields. On top of that, machines can be equipped with advanced technologies, such as GPS and sensors, to optimize planting, fertilization, and irrigation, leading to more sustainable and efficient farming practices.
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Qishloq xo'jaligida mashinalardan foydalanishning afzalliklari ko'p va oxir-oqibat samaradorlik va mahsuldorlikning oshishiga hissa qo'shadi. Birinchidan, traktorlar va kombaynlar kabi mashinalar katta maydonlarni qo'l mehnati bilan solishtirganda ancha tez qamrab oladi, bu fermerlarga ekinlarni o'z vaqtida ekish va yig'ishtirish imkonini beradi, "quyosh charaqlab turganda pichanni o'rib olish" deganidek. Bu, ayniqsa, vaqt muhim bo'lgan eng yuqori mavsumlarda juda muhimdir.

Ikkinchidan, mashinalar fermerlar va qishloq xo'jaligi ishchilarining jismoniy zo'riqishini kamaytiradi. Aks holda belni sindiradigan mehnatni talab qiladigan vazifalar mashinalar yordamida nisbatan oson bajarilishi mumkin. Bundan tashqari, zamonaviy qishloq xo'jaligi texnikasi tomonidan taqdim etiladigan aniqlik chiqindilarni minimallashtiradi va hosildorlikni maksimal darajaga yetkazadi. Bundan tashqari, mashinalar ekish, o'g'itlash va sug'orishni optimallashtirish uchun GPS va sensorlar kabi ilg'or texnologiyalar bilan jihozlanishi mumkin, bu esa yanada barqaror va samarali dehqonchilik amaliyotlariga olib keladi.

questions.prompt: Why do some farmers still harvest crops by hand?
questions.sampleA1: Hand harvesting is slow. But some farmers do it. It is hard work.
questions.sampleA2: Some farmers harvest by hand because it is tradition. It is hard, but they do it. They don't have machines.
questions.sampleB1: Some farmers still harvest crops by hand for different reasons. Sometimes they don't have enough money to buy machines. For example, in poor countries, machines are too expensive. However, some crops are delicate and machines can damage them. So, hand harvesting is necessary in those cases.
questions.sampleB2: There are a few reasons, really. For one, some land is just too steep or awkward for machinery to get onto. What's more, delicate crops like berries bruise easily, so they need a gentle human touch. And in poorer areas, hand-picking gives people jobs, which machines would simply wipe out.
questions.uzSampleA1: Qo'lda hosil yig'ish sekin. Lekin ba'zi fermerlar shunday qilishadi. Bu og'ir ish.
questions.uzSampleA2: Ba'zi fermerlar hosilni qo'lda yig'ishtiradilar, chunki bu an'ana. Bu qiyin, lekin ular shunday qilishadi. Ularda mashinalar yo'q.
questions.uzSampleB1: Ba'zi fermerlar turli sabablarga ko'ra hali ham ekinlarni qo'lda yig'ishtirib olishadi. Ba'zan ularda mashinalar sotib olishga yetarli pul bo'lmaydi. Masalan, kambag'al mamlakatlarda mashinalar juda qimmat. Biroq, ba'zi ekinlar juda nozik bo'ladi va mashinalar ularga zarar yetkazishi mumkin. Shuning uchun, bunday hollarda qo'lda yig'ishtirish zarur.
questions.uzSampleB2:
Bir qancha omillar ba'zi fermerlarning hali ham ekinlarni qo'lda yig'ishtirishda davom etishiga sabab bo'ladi. Ba'zi hollarda, yerning relyefi mashinalardan foydalanishni qiyinlashtiradi yoki imkonsiz qiladi. Tik qiyaliklar va kichik dalalar qo'l mehnatiga mosroqdir.
Qolaversa, ayrim ekinlar mashinalar ta'minlay olmaydigan nozik muomalani talab qiladi. Nozik meva va sabzavotlar ko'karish va buzilishning oldini olish uchun ko'pincha qo'lda yig'ishtiriladi.
Bundan tashqari, qo'lda hosil yig'ishtirish mahalliy aholi uchun, ayniqsa, ish imkoniyatlari cheklangan hududlarda ish o'rinlarini yaratishi mumkin.

vocabulary.title: Why do...
sentenceStarters: "Hand harvesting is necessary when..." - "Qo'lda hosil yig'ish zarur bo'ladi, qachonki..."
"It is important to consider..." - "E'tiborga olish muhimki..."

questions.sampleAnswer:
Some farmers still harvest crops by hand for a variety of reasons. Firstly, in certain regions, the terrain may be unsuitable for large machinery. Steep hillsides or small, terraced fields often necessitate manual harvesting. Secondly, some crops are too delicate to be harvested by machines without causing damage. Consider, for example, berries or certain types of vegetables that bruise easily.

Furthermore, in some communities, manual harvesting is a traditional practice passed down through generations, a labor of love. It provides employment opportunities in rural areas and supports local economies. On top of everything, for organic farming practices, manual harvesting is often preferred to avoid the use of machinery that may compact the soil or require the use of non-organic lubricants.
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Ba'zi fermerlar turli sabablarga ko'ra hali ham ekinlarni qo'lda yig'ishtirib olishadi. Birinchidan, ayrim hududlarda relyef katta texnika uchun yaroqsiz bo'lishi mumkin. Tik yonbag'irlar yoki kichik, terrasali dalalar ko'pincha qo'lda hosil yig'ishtirishni talab qiladi. Ikkinchidan, ba'zi ekinlar mashinalar tomonidan shikast yetkazmasdan yig'ishtirib olish uchun juda nozik bo'ladi. Misol uchun, tez shikastlanadigan rezavor mevalar yoki sabzavotlarning ayrim turlarini ko'rib chiqing.

Bundan tashqari, ba'zi jamoalarda qo'lda hosil yig'ishtirish avloddan-avlodga o'tib kelayotgan an'anaviy amaliyotdir, bu – mehr bilan qilinadigan ish. Bu qishloq joylarida ish bilan ta'minlash imkoniyatlarini yaratadi va mahalliy iqtisodiyotni qo'llab-quvvatlaydi. Eng muhimi, organik dehqonchilik amaliyotlari uchun qo'lda hosil yig'ishtirish ko'pincha tuproqni zichlashtirishi yoki noorganik moylash materiallaridan foydalanishni talab qilishi mumkin bo'lgan texnikadan foydalanishdan qochish uchun afzal ko'riladi.

questions.prompt: Describe a time you did a difficult physical task yourself instead of hiring someone.
questions.sampleA1: I painted my room. It was hard work. I am happy now.
questions.sampleA2: I painted my room myself. It was difficult, but I finished it. I feel good because I did it myself.
questions.sampleB1: I decided to fix my car myself instead of taking it to a mechanic. It was a difficult task and took me a long time. For example, I had to watch many videos to understand how to replace the part. However, after I finished, I felt very proud of myself. I saved money and learned something new.
questions.sampleB2: Right, so the task that springs to mind is when I decided to lay a new wooden floor in my living room myself, rather than calling in a professional fitter. To be honest, I'd never done anything like it before, so I was jumping in at the deep end. I spent a whole weekend measuring, cutting the boards, and clicking them into place, and by the end my back was absolutely killing me. It was far more fiddly and physically draining than I'd ever imagined. That said, the sense of accomplishment I got once it was finished was second to none. Every time I walked into that room, I couldn't help but feel a real surge of pride, knowing I'd pulled it off with my own two hands. There's something about physical work like that — you can actually see the fruits of your labour, which you don't always get with a desk job. It also gave me a real confidence boost, because I'd proved to myself I could take on something daunting and see it through. Having said all that, I completely understand why plenty of people would rather pay someone to do it. The thing is, time is money, and a seasoned professional can knock the job out in a fraction of the time, and probably to a higher standard. On top of that, some jobs call for specialist tools and know-how that most of us simply don't have lying around. So at the end of the day, I suppose it boils down to whether you value the money you'd save or the time you'd lose.

bulletPoints: Describe a time you did a difficult physical task yourself instead of hiring someone.
How did doing this work with your own hands increase your sense of accomplishment?
Why do some people prefer to pay for services rather than doing things themselves?
questions.sampleAnswer:
Recently, I decided to repaint my entire apartment myself rather than hiring a professional. It was a monumental task, requiring several days of preparation, countless hours of painting, and a significant amount of physical exertion. I chose to do it myself primarily to save money, but I also wanted the satisfaction of knowing I had transformed my living space with my own two hands.

The sense of accomplishment I felt after completing the job was immense. Undoubtedly, seeing the freshly painted walls, knowing I had done it all myself, gave me a profound sense of pride and ownership. It wasn't just about saving money; it was about proving to myself that I could tackle a challenging project and see it through to completion. I felt like I had moved mountains. It was also a great learning experience, as I learned new skills and techniques along the way.

However, I understand why some people prefer to pay for services rather than doing things themselves. Time is a valuable commodity, and for many, it's more efficient to outsource tasks to professionals who can complete them quickly and efficiently. Furthermore, some tasks require specialized skills or equipment that the average person may not possess. At the end of the day, it comes down to individual priorities and resources. Different strokes for different folks.
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Yaqinda men butun kvartiramni professionalni yollash o'rniga o'zim bo'yashga qaror qildim. Bu juda katta vazifa edi, bir necha kunlik tayyorgarlik, son-sanoqsiz soatlik bo'yash va sezilarli jismoniy kuch talab qildi. Men buni, asosan, pulni tejash uchun o'zim qilishni tanladim, lekin o'z qo'llarim bilan yashash joyimni o'zgartirganimni bilishdan ham qoniqishni xohladim.

Ishni tugatgandan so'ng his qilgan yutuq tuyg'usi juda katta edi. Shubhasiz, yangi bo'yalgan devorlarni ko'rish, bularning hammasini o'zim qilganimni bilish, menga chuqur g'urur va egalik hissini berdi. Gap faqat pulni tejashda emas edi; gap o'zimga qiyin loyihani uddalay olishimni va uni oxirigacha yetkazishimni isbotlashda edi. Men tog'larni ko'chirgandek his qildim. Bu, shuningdek, ajoyib o'rganish tajribasi bo'ldi, chunki men yo'l davomida yangi ko'nikmalar va texnikalarni o'rgandim.

Biroq, men nega ba'zi odamlar o'zlari qilishdan ko'ra xizmatlar uchun pul to'lashni afzal ko'rishlarini tushunaman. Vaqt qimmatli narsa va ko'pchilik uchun vazifalarni tez va samarali bajaradigan professionallarga topshirish ancha samaraliroq. Bundan tashqari, ba'zi vazifalar o'rtacha odamda bo'lmasligi mumkin bo'lgan maxsus ko'nikmalar yoki uskunalar talab qiladi. Oxir oqibat, hamma narsa individual ustuvorliklar va resurslarga bog'liq. Har kimning o'z didi bor.

questions.sampleA1: Libraries are good. They have books. Books are free.
questions.sampleA2: Libraries have books and computers. They are free, but some people don't go. Libraries are important because everyone can read.
questions.sampleB1: Public libraries are very important. They give people free books to read. For example, students can use them for studying. However, some people say libraries are not needed anymore because we have the internet. Also, libraries cost a lot of money to keep open.
questions.sampleB2: Public libraries are definitely a topic worth chewing over, and I can see where both sides are coming from. On the one hand, there's a strong case for them. First and foremost, they offer free access to books and information, which is a real lifeline for anyone who can't afford to buy their own or doesn't have the internet at home. They also do a brilliant job of getting kids into reading from an early age. On top of that, they double up as community hubs — quiet study spaces, free workshops, a warm place to sit — which you can't really put a price on. On the other hand, I suppose some people would argue that libraries are becoming a bit outdated. The thing is, most of us now have the whole world at our fingertips online, and e-books are catching on fast. Running a library doesn't come cheap either — the buildings, the staff, the upkeep all cost a small fortune, and if footfall is dropping, it's fair to ask whether that money could be put to better use elsewhere. That said, if you ask me, libraries still have a vital part to play. I don't buy the idea that they're past their prime. Not everyone has a laptop or wants to stare at a screen all day, and there's something irreplaceable about browsing physical shelves. What libraries need to do is move with the times — lend e-books, offer computer access, run digital classes — so they stay relevant. At the end of the day, they're far more than just rooms full of books.

against: Most people use digital resources today.

questions.sampleAnswer:
Public libraries are a valuable resource, especially in today's digital age, although there are valid arguments against their continued importance. On the one hand, libraries provide free access to books, which is crucial for promoting literacy and lifelong learning. They encourage reading habits, particularly among children and young adults, and offer a quiet study place for students and researchers. To boot, libraries often host community events and workshops, serving as hubs for social interaction and cultural enrichment.

However, it is true that many people now rely on digital resources for information and entertainment. The internet offers instant access to a vast amount of knowledge, and e-books are becoming increasingly popular. Furthermore, maintaining libraries can be costly, requiring significant investment in infrastructure, staffing, and resources. Not everyone visits libraries regularly, so some argue that the money could be better spent on other public services.

Ultimately, I believe that public libraries still have an important role to play in society. They provide a valuable service to those who may not have access to digital resources or who prefer the tactile experience of reading a physical book. Libraries can adapt to the changing times by offering digital resources and services, such as e-book lending and computer access, while continuing to provide a welcoming and inclusive space for all members of the community. You can't judge a book by its cover, and you can't dismiss libraries just because technology is advancing. They must evolve to remain relevant.
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Ommaviy kutubxonalar qimmatli resurs hisoblanadi, ayniqsa bugungi raqamli davrda, garchi ularning davomiy ahamiyatiga qarshi asosli dalillar mavjud bo'lsa ham. Bir tomondan, kutubxonalar kitoblarga bepul kirishni ta'minlaydi, bu esa savodxonlikni va umrbod ta'limni rivojlantirish uchun juda muhimdir. Ular o'qish odatlarini rag'batlantiradi, xususan bolalar va yoshlar orasida, va talabalar va tadqiqotchilar uchun tinch o'qish joyini taklif etadi. Qolaversa, kutubxonalar ko'pincha jamoat tadbirlari va seminarlarini o'tkazadi, ijtimoiy aloqa va madaniy boyitish markazlari vazifasini bajaradi.

Biroq, ko'p odamlar hozirda ma'lumot va ko'ngilochar maqsadlarda raqamli resurslarga tayanayotgani rost. Internet bilimning ulkan miqdoriga tezkor kirishni taklif etadi va elektron kitoblar tobora ommalashib bormoqda. Bundan tashqari, kutubxonalarni saqlash qimmatga tushishi mumkin, bu infratuzilma, xodimlar va resurslarga katta sarmoya kiritishni talab qiladi. Hamma ham kutubxonalarga muntazam ravishda tashrif buyurmaydi, shuning uchun ba'zilarning fikricha, bu pulni boshqa davlat xizmatlariga sarflash yaxshiroq bo'lar edi.

Yakuniy xulosa shuki, men ommaviy kutubxonalar jamiyatda hali ham muhim rol o'ynashi kerak, deb hisoblayman. Ular raqamli resurslarga kirish imkoniga ega bo'lmagan yoki jismoniy kitobni o'qishning taktil tajribasini afzal ko'rganlar uchun qimmatli xizmat ko'rsatadi. Kutubxonalar raqamli resurslar va xizmatlarni, masalan, elektron kitoblarni berish va kompyuterga kirishni taklif qilish orqali o'zgaruvchan zamonga moslasha oladi, shu bilan birga jamiyatning barcha a'zolari uchun qulay va inklyuziv joyni ta'minlashda davom etadi. Kitobni muqovasiga qarab baholab bo'lmaydi, texnologiya rivojlanayotgani uchun ham kutubxonalarni rad etib bo'lmaydi. Ular dolzarb bo'lib qolish uchun rivojlanishi kerak.
